The short answer: Dyson builds the better dryer. Laifen is the better buy for most Canadians. The gap that matters is not performance — both move high airflow at lower heat — it is price and proven reliability. In Canada a Dyson Supersonic starts at about C$400 against about C$100 for the Laifen Air, roughly a 4× gap. Our data does not show Laifen is unreliable; it shows Laifen’s reliability is unproven, because the brand is young. Whether that trade is worth it depends entirely on how much a failure at month six would cost you.

Price in Canada: Laifen vs Dyson

The Laifen Air costs about C$100 and the cheapest Dyson Supersonic costs about C$400 — a 4× gap. The Supersonic Nural is 6.3×.

What you are paying for with Dyson. Not airflow. Both brands describe the same fundamental approach: a high-speed motor moving a large volume of air at a lower temperature, rather than a hot element blasting heat. The Dyson premium buys brand equity, a genuine engineering reputation, a Canadian service network, and the confidence of a product family that has been on sale for a decade.

What you are paying for with Laifen. About a quarter of the price for the same core approach, in a package rated 4.5 stars from 278 Canadian buyers. Laifen’s contribution to this category was making high-speed drying accessible rather than aspirational.

A practical way to think about it:

If you…Buy
Want the lowest risk of an unresolved failureDyson
Want the best drying experience per dollarLaifen
Travel internationally and need universal voltageDyson Supersonic Travel
Are replacing a C$30 dryer and want a real upgradeLaifen Air
Have thick or long hair and a flexible budgetLaifen SE2, or Dyson Supersonic

Drying performance: Laifen vs Dyson

Both brands use the same underlying approach, and that approach is the right one for most hair.

  • High airflow at lower heat, rather than a hot element doing the work (manufacturer claim, both brands)
  • Airflow was the most-discussed topic in our entire dataset at 1,585 mentions — more than noise, weight, price or durability in raw mention volume Review analysis
  • The complaint pattern in that topic is one-directional: reviewers rarely complain a dryer is too powerful; they complain it is too weak for their hair Review analysis
  • Underpowered dryers are the most common single reason reviewers describe returning a dryer Review analysis

What we cannot tell you. We have not measured airflow or dry time on any of these four models. Any specific second-count you read in a comparison like this one is either measured by someone with a bench, or invented. We will publish measured numbers on our Lab Test Card as each unit completes our protocol.

Practical guidance: if drying speed is your priority and your hair is thick or long, buy the higher-airflow model in either family — the Laifen SE2 at about C$145 or the Dyson Supersonic at about C$400.

Weight and handling: Laifen vs Dyson

Weight is the third most-discussed topic in our dataset at 1,318 mentions, and 73% of that discussion is positive — buyers notice when a dryer is light.

  • Dyson Supersonic Travel is designed as a lighter, more compact variant of the Supersonic Manufacturer claim
  • Laifen Air is positioned as “ultra light” in its listing title Manufacturer claim
  • The Laifen SE2 is heavier than the Air, and reviewers of step-up models across the category frequently note the extra weight Review analysis

Why this matters more than it sounds. A hair dryer is held at arm’s length for 5–15 minutes. Weight complaints in our dataset cluster around longer hair and longer sessions. If you dry your hair daily and take more than ten minutes, weight should be a higher priority in your decision than peak airflow.

One number worth having: a 100 g difference at arm’s length feels meaningfully heavier over a ten-minute session. We will publish measured weight with cord, and the hand-held section separately, for all four models.

Heat control: Laifen vs Dyson

Heat and safety issues were the second-largest complaint cluster in our dataset, with 590 negative mentions on temperature and overheating.

  • Dyson Supersonic Nural adds heat sensing, which is the most advanced heat-control approach in this comparison Manufacturer claim
  • Both Laifen models use smart temperature control rather than fixed heat steps Manufacturer claim
  • 182 mentions of smoking or catching fire appear in our dataset, 96% of them negative reviews. This is the most reliably negative signal we found Review analysis
  • 215 mentions of burning or plastic smell, 84% negative. A persistent burning smell is the most common precursor reviewers describe before a dryer dies Review analysis

The honest read: heat-control technology is a genuine differentiator, and it is one of the areas where Dyson’s engineering investment shows. But the failures our data captures are mostly hardware — cord, switch, element — not control logic. Better heat control does not protect you from a cord that fails at the handle junction.

For fine or thin hair, heat control matters more than airflow, because the failure mode reviewers describe is scorching rather than slow drying Review analysis.

Noise: Laifen vs Dyson

Noise appears in 848 reviews in our dataset, 10.3% of the total, and 33% of those mentions are negative.

  • Neither brand publishes a measured sound pressure figure at a stated distance Manufacturer claim
  • Marketing terms such as “low noise” and “quiet” appear on both Laifen and Dyson listings without a measurement to back them Manufacturer claim
  • Noise was the fourth most-mentioned concern in our dataset, behind airflow, usability and size Review analysis

What we will publish. Sound pressure at 30 cm and at 1 metre, against a recorded background level, using the same meter for every unit. Until then, treat every “quiet” claim in this category as unverified.

Attachments and diffusers: Laifen vs Dyson

Attachment security is a small topic with an unusually high complaint ratio — 186 mentions, 57% of them negative.

  • Both brands use magnetic attachments Manufacturer claim
  • Only the Laifen SE2 and Dyson Supersonic Nural clearly include a diffuser at this price point; the Air and Supersonic Travel vary by variant Amazon.ca data
  • “The nozzle keeps falling off” and “the concentrator does not stay on” are recurring phrasings in our attachment complaints Review analysis
  • One reviewer described a nozzle that had melted where it sat against the barrel Buyer feedback

If you have curly or wavy hair, a diffuser is effectively mandatory, and attachment security is the specific thing to check. Our curly hair guide covers the detail.

Travel and storage: Laifen vs Dyson

This is the one category where Dyson wins clearly, and it is not close.

  • Dyson Supersonic Travel uses universal voltage, which makes it usable in Europe, the UK and Australia with only a plug adapter Manufacturer claim
  • Neither Laifen model is dual voltage Manufacturer claim
  • Voltage was the single most-discussed topic in our entire dataset at 785 mentions — ahead of noise, weight and price Review analysis

If you travel internationally more than once a year, the Dyson Supersonic Travel’s universal voltage is worth real money, because the alternative is buying a second dryer abroad or carrying a heavy voltage converter. Our travel hair dryer guide covers the alternatives at lower prices, including the Dreame Pocket Pro.

Durability and warranty: Laifen vs Dyson

This is the section that should decide your purchase, and it is the one most comparison articles skip.

Where that leaves this comparison. The Laifen Air at about C$100 and SE2 at about C$145 both sit in the better quality band, and Dyson at about C$400–629.99 sits in it too. On price band alone, neither is disadvantaged.

What we genuinely cannot tell you is whether Laifen’s failure rate is higher than Dyson’s. Laifen’s oldest Canadian listing in our dataset has been on sale for 11 months; Dyson’s has been on sale far longer as a product family. Anyone claiming long-term reliability parity or disparity between these two brands without a multi-year dataset is guessing.

The failure mode that matters most here is hardware, not the motor:

Failure modeMentions
Stopped working entirely601

Switch or button failure300

Practical consequence: Dyson’s advantage is not that it will not fail — it is that when it does, there is a Canadian service network and a decade of process behind the warranty. That is what the extra C$300 buys. Whether it is worth C$300 is a personal risk decision, not a technical one.

Value over time: Laifen vs Dyson

The honest maths, using our data rather than assumptions.

Assume the category median failure time of 5.5 months applies to a cheap dryer and that a premium dryer lasts longer — the price-band complaint rates support that direction, with 9.6% over C$120 against 30.3% under C$50.

ScenarioCostYears of serviceCost per year
Laifen Air, replaced onceabout C$200~3 years~C$67
Laifen Air, replaced twiceabout C$300~4 years~C$75
Dyson Supersonic Travelabout C$4005+ years (expected, unverified)~C$80
Dyson Supersonic Nuralabout C$6305+ years (expected, unverified)~C$126

Read this table with care — the Dyson column assumes a service life we have not verified. What the table does show is that at one replacement, Laifen’s cost per year is roughly comparable to Dyson’s. The difference is that Laifen’s cost is a replacement purchase, and Dyson’s is a prepayment for a warranty network.

Who should buy Laifen

Buy Laifen if:

  • Your budget is under C$200 and you want real high-speed drying rather than a legacy-brand compromise
  • You are comfortable treating a hair dryer as a two-to-three year item
  • You want a brand-operated Canadian listing with one seller and one warranty counterparty
  • You have thick or long hair — the SE2 at about C$145 is tuned for exactly that buyer
  • You want to avoid paying 4× for the same fundamental airflow approach

Do not buy Laifen if:

  • A failure at month six would be a serious financial problem for you
  • You travel internationally and need universal voltage
  • You want a decade of Canadian service history behind the warranty
  • You want the most advanced heat control available

Check price for the Laifen Air at Amazon.ca · Check price for the Laifen SE2 · Read our full Laifen guide

Who should buy Dyson

Buy Dyson if:

  • Reliability risk matters more to you than price, and you want a Canadian service network behind the warranty
  • You travel internationally — the Supersonic Travel’s universal voltage solves a real problem
  • Your hair is fine, damaged or colour-treated, where the Nural’s heat sensing is the more conservative approach
  • You want the product family with the longest track record in the category
  • A 4× price premium is not a meaningful constraint

Do not buy Dyson if:

  • You are replacing a C$30 dryer and want to know whether the category is worth investing in — buy Laifen first
  • You mainly want fast drying under C$200
  • You expect a measurable difference in airflow, because both brands describe the same high-airflow, lower-heat approach

Laifen vs Dyson: alternatives worth considering

If neither of these fits, three others in our dataset are worth a look.

  • Shark SpeedStyle Pro at about C$200 — sits between Laifen and Dyson on price, with a scalp shield and a styling suite. See our Shark vs Dyson comparison
  • Dreame Pocket Pro at about C$160 — the highest-rated dryer above C$120 in our dataset at 4.6 stars, and dual voltage. The strongest Laifen alternative if travel matters
  • Slopehill 1902 at about C$43 — the highest-volume dryer in Canada at roughly 8,660 units a month. Budget quality band, so treat it as a shorter-term purchase

Laifen vs Dyson: FAQ

Is Laifen as good as Dyson? On airflow approach and features it is close. On build quality and long-term reliability Dyson is ahead, and it has a decade of service history Laifen does not. The price gap is roughly 4×, and that gap is the entire question — our data does not show Laifen is unreliable, only that its reliability is unproven.

Why is Dyson so much more expensive than Laifen? In Canada the Dyson Supersonic Travel is about C$400 and the Supersonic Nural is about C$630, against about C$100 for the Laifen Air. Dyson carries a decade of brand equity, a genuine engineering reputation and a Canadian service network. Whether that is worth 4× depends on how you weigh the risk of a failure at month six.

Which is better for thick or long hair, Laifen or Dyson? Both move high airflow at lower heat, which is the right approach for dense hair. Laifen’s SE2 at about C$145 is tuned for buyers who return dryers for being underpowered. Airflow was the most-discussed topic in our dataset at 1,585 mentions, so if drying speed is your priority, neither will disappoint.

Does Laifen break more often than Dyson? We cannot say, and anyone who claims otherwise without long-term data is guessing. What we can say is that across 8,261 Canadian reviews the median reported failure was 5.5 months, and that dryers over C$120 had a 9.6% complaint rate against 30.3% under C$50. Laifen sits in the better band.

Should I buy Laifen or save for Dyson? If a failure at month six would be a serious financial annoyance, buy Dyson — you are paying for a service network. If you are comfortable treating a C$100 dryer as a two-to-three year consumable, Laifen gives you roughly the same drying experience for a quarter of the price.

Is Laifen a real Dyson alternative or just a copy? It is a genuine brushless high-speed dryer with its own engineering, not a clone. Both use high airflow at lower heat rather than blasting hot air. Laifen’s weakness is service history and Canadian parts availability, not the technology.

Our verdict on Laifen vs Dyson

Dyson is the better dryer. Laifen is the better buy for most Canadians.

That is not a contradiction. Dyson’s advantages are real: a decade of engineering, a Canadian service network, universal voltage on the Travel model, and the Nural’s heat sensing. If a failure at month six would be a genuine problem for you, the C$300 premium buys you an answer.

But the performance gap is narrower than the price gap. Both brands describe the same high-airflow, lower-heat approach, and both sit in the price band where our data shows complaint rates falling to 9.6% from 30.3%.

Our pick for value: the Laifen Air at about C$100. Our pick if reliability outweighs price: the Dyson Supersonic.
